name: Shredder
description: Draggable list of cards that can be fed into a paper shredder slit at the bottom, turning into falling curled strips drawn on a canvas, with drag reordering and optional self-playing demo.
contents: Vertical stack of caller-rendered item cards
Shredder slit bar near the bottom
Canvas area under the slit where shredded strips fall and pile up
behavior: Items can be dragged to reorder, with a tilt and lift while held
Dragging an item into the slit feeds it through and shreds it into curled strips
Delete or Backspace on a focused item shreds it
With autoFeed the item is pulled through the slit automatically once dropped past the bite point
Shredded items are revived and loop back when loop or loopAfterDelete is set
autoAnimate shreds items one by one on its own and revives them when the list is empty
Item images are prefetched as data URLs to rasterize them for the shred effect
editableByProps: Items and how each card looks through renderItem
Width, height, inset, gap, slit and fall area sizes
Feed speed, bite distance, strip width, curl, drag tilt and lift
Auto feed, auto demo, looping and disabled state

needsCodeEdit.change: Change how fast strips fall or how bouncy the pile is
needsCodeEdit.where: STACK_K and STACK_C constants at the top of the file
STAGGER constant at the top of the file

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the delay and pacing of the autoAnimate demo
needsCodeEdit.where: The wait calls inside play() in the autoAnimate useEffect

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the overflow of the strip canvas beyond the card width
needsCodeEdit.where: OVER constant at the top of the file

fixed: Each item must have a unique id, and items must be same-origin or CORS-enabled for images to shred correctly
renderItem is required, the component throws without it
Fetches item image URLs with CORS to rasterize them for shredding
Fixed height frame, items beyond the height are clipped above the slit
Relies on pointer events and drag, so it needs touch and mouse input, and Delete or Backspace for keyboard
Width is capped at 100% of the parent so it fits small screens, but height is fixed in pixels
Strip physics, stagger and entry timings are hardcoded constants
Respects prefers-reduced-motion in its helper logic
